- `ResolutionContext` holds `Arc<GlobalSourceData>`, `Arc<ImportResolutionMap>`, `Arc<Resolver>` (the `oxc_resolver` instance) — cheap to clone, shared read-only across every worker thread.
- `ResolveState` (`types/global.rs:19`) is constructed fresh per `resolve_component` call via `ResolveState::default()` and threaded through every recursive call by `&mut` reference. It is **never** shared across components and carries no `Arc` — it's pure per-call mutable scratch state (visited-set, diagnostics accumulator, in-scope type params). If a future change tried to hoist `ResolveState` up to be shared across the rayon `.map()` (e.g. to dedupe diagnostics), that would silently corrupt cycle detection across unrelated components — the visited-set has no per-component reset mechanism, and two components racing on the same shared set would each see the other's visited entries and wrongly short-circuit.

## The three-tier data model this resolver operates on

- `CollectedType` / `CollectedTypeAlias` — what the extractor produced: structural, not yet resolved, may reference cross-file names.
- `PropType` — resolved output type at the *type level* (an interface reference becomes a bare `PropType::Named`, never expanded here).
- `ResolvedChain` (`resolver/mod.rs`) — resolved output at the *chain/component level*: `props: Vec<ParsedProp>`, `inheritance: Vec<InheritedLayer>`, `composes: Vec<String>`, `discriminant_prop: Option<String>`. This is the accumulator a props-providing type (interface, intersection, discriminated union) produces; it's private to the resolver module (`struct ResolvedChain`, not `pub`).

**Invariant 1 — an interface name resolves differently depending on which level asked.** At the type level (`resolve_named`, called for a *field's* type — e.g. `value: SomeInterface`), a matched interface returns `PropType::Named { name, args }` — bare, unexpanded. At the chain level (`resolve_props_chain`, called for a *props-base* type — the component's own props type, or an `extends` target), the same interface expands via `resolve_interface_chain` into real `ParsedProp`s. This split exists because a field whose type happens to be an interface should show as a named type reference in RDT-compatible output, not get flattened into an anonymous object — but a component's *own* props type (or something it extends) must actually contribute fields. Conflating the two would either over-expand nested interface-typed fields into inline objects, or under-expand a component's own extends chain.

## Locked design decision: source-before-known-pattern precedence (P0-1)

`resolver/precedence.rs`'s `resolve_source_defined_or_known` is the **only** place either `chain.rs` or `named.rs` may implement "how does a bare type name resolve." It checks, in this exact order:

1. `resolve_to_canonical` — follow imports/re-exports/barrel files to the real declaring `(file, name)`.
2. `lookup_type_alias` at that canonical location.
3. `lookup_interface` at that canonical location.
4. `resolve_known` — the hardcoded library-pattern shortcut table in `known.rs` (SxProps, VariantProps, HTMLChakraProps, …).

**Why this order, and why it's locked:** a project can legitimately declare its own `interface SxProps { customSx: string }` that has nothing to do with MUI. If `known.rs`'s hardcoded SxProps shortcut were checked before the project's own source, that project-defined interface would be silently replaced by the opaque MUI shortcut — the component's real, resolvable prop (`customSx`) would vanish with no trace. `named.rs` always had this order right and documented it as intentional. `chain.rs`'s `extends`-clause path (used when a project's `interface Foo extends SomeName`) independently re-implemented the same sequence and got it backwards — checking `resolve_known` *before* the project's own interface/alias lookup. Nothing tied the two orderings together, so `chain.rs` was free to drift the moment it was written (see `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` §8). This is the confirmed P0-1 bug; `precedence.rs` was extracted specifically to make that drift structurally impossible — both call sites now share one function, so reordering one without the other can't happen again.

A regression test locks this at both the shared-function level (`precedence.rs`'s `source_defined_interface_wins_over_a_known_pattern_shortcut`) and end-to-end through the extends path (`mod.rs`'s `test_extends_clause_prefers_project_defined_sx_props_over_known_shortcut`).

**Documented residual divergence (not a bug, but don't call the two functions "unified"):** `chain.rs` and `named.rs` still differ in two respects the P0-1 fix didn't touch — `named.rs` checks React-builtin status *before* canonical resolution, `chain.rs` checks it *after* the known-pattern block; and `chain.rs` checks `is_ts_utility_type` very early (step 1, before known-pattern), while `named.rs`'s analogous check runs last (step 6, after interface/alias/known-pattern). Neither divergence reproduces the P0-1 shape (a user-defined type being shadowed by a shortcut), so they were explicitly left out of scope. If a future change touches either ordering, re-verify this claim rather than assuming it's still accurate — the flagging note lives in `root-cause-analysis.md` §8, not in code.

## Locked design decision: `give_up` vs `new` for `OpaqueDetail`

`PropType::Opaque`'s payload (`OpaqueDetail`, `types/output.rs:324`) is private outside its own module and has exactly two constructors:

- `OpaqueDetail::give_up(state: &mut ResolveState, raw, reason, diagnostic)` — pushes `diagnostic` onto `state.diagnostics` *and* builds the value in one call. This is the sanctioned path for every real resolver call site (`collected.rs`, `chain.rs`, `named.rs`, `func.rs`, `primitives.rs`, `template.rs`) — a call site literally cannot construct an opaque value without being forced to also explain why, at the same call site, so "degrade silently" is not an available mistake to make there.
- `OpaqueDetail::new(raw, reason)` — builds the value with **no** diagnostic push. Used exclusively by `known.rs`.

**Why the split exists:** `known.rs` has no `ResolveState` to push into — and per the top-level `CLAUDE.md`'s "no reverse dependencies" rule (`resolver` depends on `types`/`known`, never the other way), `known.rs` must not depend on `resolver::ResolveState` just to gain a diagnostics channel. So `known.rs` builds bare `OpaqueDetail`s via `new`, and the *caller* (`chain.rs` step 2 / `named.rs` step 5, both of which do have a live `ResolveState`) is responsible for detecting `KnownPatternResult::Type(PropType::Opaque(detail))` and calling `known::push_known_opaque_diagnostic(&mut state.diagnostics, detail.reason(), type_name, file)` right after. This was itself a fixed gap (an adversarial-review finding, tests `test_known_opaque_result_emits_diagnostic_at_type_level` / `_at_chain_level`) — a `KnownPatternResult::Type` that happened to be `Opaque` (ThemingProps, StylesApiProps, cva/tv without discoverable variants) used to degrade with zero diagnostic, unlike every other opaque-producing path. **Invariant 2:** any new `known.rs` match arm that can return `KnownPatternResult::Type(PropType::Opaque(_))` relies on both call sites' existing post-match check to surface it — a third call site into `resolve_known` that skips this check would silently reintroduce the exact bug the two existing tests guard against.

## Cycle detection: scope and limits

`resolve_props_chain` (chain.rs) is the only place with an explicit visited-set check:

```rust
let visit_key = format!("{}:{}<{}>", consuming_file, type_name, type_args.join(","));
if !state.visited.insert(visit_key) { return ResolvedChain::give_up(...) }
```

**Invariant 3 — the visited key is `(file, type_name, type_args)`, not `(file, type_name)` alone.** This was a real bug (see `test_two_distinct_partial_extends_targets_both_resolve`): `interface TableProps extends Partial<RowHeights>, Partial<ColumnWidths>` needs both `Partial<RowHeights>` and `Partial<ColumnWidths>` to resolve independently. A bare-name visited key would treat the second `Partial<...>` as "already visited" (colliding on `"Partial"`) and silently drop `ColumnWidths`'s contribution with zero diagnostic. Any future change to the visit-key construction must preserve `type_args` in the key or this regression returns.

**What this cycle detection catches, and what it doesn't:**
- It catches genuine self-reference at the *chain* level: an interface's `extends` clause (directly or transitively) referencing itself (`test_self_referential_extends_emits_diagnostic_instead_of_silent_default`), and a props-base type alias cycling back to itself.
- It does **not** catch cycles at the *named-type* level (`resolve_named` in `named.rs`) — that function has no visited-set of its own. A field-level cycle (e.g. `type A = { self: B }; type B = { self: A }` referenced only as field types, never as a props base) is instead bounded only by `MAX_DEPTH`, not detected as "circular" with the more specific diagnostic — it degrades to a `MaxDepthExceeded` opaque once depth runs out, without ever getting the `DiagnosticCode::MaxDepthExceeded`-with-circular-reference-hint treatment the chain-level path gets pre-emptively. This is a real asymmetry, not an oversight documented anywhere else — a future contributor "fixing" `resolve_named` to add its own visited-set would need to reconcile it with the fact that fields legitimately reference the same interface repeatedly in siblings without that being a cycle (e.g. two props both typed `Theme`), so any fix needs *reference identity* awareness, not blanket revisit-once semantics.
- Branch-local cycle detection: `resolve_union_alias` (alias.rs) and the `Omit<T, keyof U>` structural handling both clone `state.visited` into a throwaway `branch_state` before probing a union member or a `keyof` operand, then merge only the diagnostics back — never the visited-set. This is deliberate: a union member (or the `U` in `Omit<T, keyof U> & U`) is very often *also* resolved for real elsewhere in the same alias, and sharing the main visited-set would mark it "already visited" during the branch probe and make the real, later resolution come back empty. **Invariant 4:** any new speculative/probing resolution (resolving something just to inspect its shape, not to keep its output) must clone `state.visited` into a branch-local `ResolveState`, never mutate the shared one — this is the established idiom, not incidental to these two call sites.

## `MAX_DEPTH` — purpose and how it differs from the extractor's guard

`MAX_DEPTH: u8 = 20` in `resolver/mod.rs` bounds *recursive resolution depth* — every recursive entry point (`resolve_props_chain`, `resolve_named`, `resolve_collected_type`) checks `depth > MAX_DEPTH` and degrades to an opaque `MaxDepthExceeded` diagnostic via the shared `max_depth_diagnostic` helper. This exists to bound **type-graph traversal depth** — how many named-type hops (interface → extends → interface → alias → …) resolution will follow before giving up — which is a different axis than the extractor's `MAX_SOURCE_NESTING_DEPTH` (mentioned in `template.rs`'s doc comment as an analogous guard), which bounds **source-AST nesting depth** during a single file's parse (e.g. deeply nested object/array literal syntax in one type expression). A pathological type could be shallow in source-AST terms but deep in resolution-graph terms (a long `extends` chain across many files) or vice versa (one file with deeply nested inline object types but no cross-type references at all) — the two guards are not interchangeable and both are needed. `MAX_DEPTH` is deliberately `u8` (max 255), reinforcing that 20 is a "this smells like a cycle, not a legitimately deep type" threshold, not a hard safety ceiling sized for worst-case input.

A separate, unrelated cap exists in `template.rs`: `MAX_TEMPLATE_LITERAL_EXPANSIONS = 4096`, bounding the Cartesian product of a template literal's per-part alternatives (each part can be a union with many members, so the product is exponential in part count) — this is a *combinatorial* guard, not a recursion-depth guard, and uses the same "cap, then degrade to Opaque with a diagnostic" shape as `MAX_DEPTH` without being the same mechanism.

## Generic substitution: what works, what's known-incomplete

`substitute.rs` implements **purely structural** substitution for user-defined generic type aliases (`type Assign<T, U> = Omit<T, keyof U> & U`) — no type inference, no conditional-type evaluation. Two entry points:

- `apply_generic_args` — call-site arguments arrive as *display strings* (`type_args: &[String]`, the chain-level resolution path's historical shape) and get recovered into `CollectedType` on a best-effort basis via `raw_arg_to_collected_type`, which only recognizes plain identifiers and quoted string literals — anything with nested generics, unions, etc. is preserved as an opaque `CollectedType::Raw` string, not actually substituted.
- `generic_alias_with_structured_args` — used when the caller already has a *structured* `CollectedType` argument (e.g. `SelectRootBaseProps<T>` passed as another generic alias's own argument) — skips the string round-trip entirely, so nested generics and `keyof` operands survive substitution intact. `resolve_base_as_chain` (alias.rs) prefers this path when available, falling back to the string-based path only when arguments are already flattened to display strings.

**Invariant 5:** `build_substitution` silently drops trailing unfilled type parameters when a call site under-applies a generic alias (`Foo<string>` for `type Foo<T, U> = ...` — `U` is left unsubstituted) but as of the current code **does** push a `DiagnosticCode::GenericArgumentMismatch` warning naming the unfilled params (test: `build_substitution_diagnoses_unfilled_trailing_type_params`) — this was fixed from an earlier fully-silent version; `root-cause-analysis.md`'s standalone-findings table still describes the pre-fix "silently truncates" behavior and is stale on this specific point relative to current code. Verify against the live diagnostic before citing that table entry as still-open.

**Known, documented incomplete case — Ariakit's `Props<T, O>` pattern.** `docs/benchmarks.md` root-causes 6 of 10 outlier components (Ariakit, ark-ui, storybook-emotion, fluentui) in one benchmark corpus to generic-alias substitution not matching the pattern *at all* — further upstream than anything `substitute.rs` currently handles. Ariakit's own shape is `type Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>`, requiring substituting `T = "button"` through a *nested* `Omit` + `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` chain where `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` itself is a React builtin needing its own args substituted before it can resolve to an `HtmlAttributes` shape. The existing machinery handles single-level generic aliases whose body is directly `Omit<T, keyof U> & U` (covered by `test_generic_type_alias_substitution`); it does not yet chase a generic parameter through an intermediate builtin generic. This is an open gap, not a design decision — don't read the existing substitution machinery as "handles generics," it handles one well-tested shape of generics.

## Give-up discipline: `ResolvedChain`'s two "this contributes nothing" constructors

Mirroring the `OpaqueDetail` split at the chain level: `ResolvedChain::empty()` is the base accumulator every real resolution path builds up from (interface chain resolution, extends merging). `ResolvedChain::empty_with_compose(type_name)` and `ResolvedChain::give_up(type_name, diag, state)` are the two sanctioned "this type contributes nothing further" signals — `give_up` additionally pushes a diagnostic first. **Invariant 6:** every give-up path in `chain.rs`/`alias.rs` must go through one of these two, never a bare `ResolvedChain::default()` — a bare `default()` was itself a fixed bug (`test_self_referential_extends_emits_diagnostic_instead_of_silent_default`, `test_literal_union_as_props_base_emits_diagnostic_instead_of_silent_default`): the cycle-detected branch and the literal-union-as-props-base branch both used to return a silent empty chain with no trace. `composes` — react-docgen's own field for "props come from this type, named instead of flattened" — is populated by every give-up path today specifically so a degraded resolution still surfaces *something* in RDT-compatible output rather than silently vanishing to zero props.

## Known gaps (cross-referenced, not re-derived)

These are documented elsewhere and intentionally not re-litigated here:

- **Generic substitution through nested builtin chains** (Ariakit `Props<T, O>` and 5 siblings) — `docs/benchmarks.md`, "Corsa-deferred" generic-parameter-substitution item.
- **`composes` as a stop-gap, not a fix** — `docs/benchmarks.md` explains `composes` population closes the *symptom* (silent zero-props output) for type-checker-boundary failures, not the underlying inability to expand conditional/mapped/indexed-access types without a real checker.
- **Resolver precedence's two residual (non-P0-1) divergences** between `chain.rs` and `named.rs` (React-builtin-check ordering, `is_ts_utility_type` check ordering) — `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` §8, explicitly flagged as open follow-up, not fixed by the P0-1 precedence extraction.
- **`resolve_named`'s lack of its own cycle-detection visited-set** (this document's Invariant 3 discussion) — not tracked in either doc today; flagging here as a genuine gap surfaced while writing this file, worth a follow-up note in `root-cause-analysis.md` if a future audit revisits cycle detection.

## Other structural notes worth knowing before touching this code

- **`AtFile` is a substitution-tracking marker, not a resolvable type.** `CollectedType::AtFile { file, inner }` says "`inner` was written in `file`, not whatever file this call chain has been resolving relative to" — created when a generic argument is substituted from the caller's scope into a callee alias declared elsewhere. Every dispatch site (`resolve_base_as_chain`, `resolve_collected_type`, `substitute_type`) must switch file context to `file` before recursing into `inner`, or same-file lookups silently resolve against the wrong file.
- **Union alias members resolve relative to the alias's *own* declaring file, not the caller's consuming file** (`resolve_type_alias_type`'s doc comment, `test_union_alias_members_resolve_relative_to_alias_own_file_not_caller`). A `type Combined = A | B` alias imported cross-file still has `A`/`B` as same-file siblings of `Combined` wherever `Combined` itself is declared — using the caller's file produces spurious "Cannot resolve type 'A'" diagnostics for names that were never meant to be looked up relative to the importer.
- **A generic interface/alias's own declared type parameters must be registered before its body is resolved**, via `ctx.global.interface_type_params` / `type_alias_params` feeding `state.in_scope_type_params` — otherwise `TData`, `T`, `U`, etc. read as unresolvable named types with a spurious warning instead of being recognized as expected, unexpandable placeholders (`test_generic_interface_own_type_params_suppress_diagnostic`).
- **Curated vs Full vs None `HtmlAttributeMode`** changes *where* HTML-attribute expansion happens, not whether an `InheritedLayer` is recorded — in Curated mode `resolve_component` synthesizes a small curated subset (`notable_inherited`) from `react_types::notable_html_attrs`; in Full mode `extends.rs`'s `real_html_attrs_chain` looks up the actually-merged `@types/react` interface and expands it for real into own props; in None mode neither happens. This is orthogonal to the resolver's normal source-vs-known precedence — it's a pipeline-level configuration knob threaded through `ResolutionContext`, not a resolution-order decision.

These two strings normally agree, but can diverge for a src_dir reached through a symlink (see the negative pair below), so 'full path' throughout this criterion means that pre-canonicalization walk-emitted string specifically. Given a PipelineOptions.src_dirs containing one or more directories that exist on disk, extract() returns an ExtractionOutput whose components include every React component declared in every .ts/.tsx file reachable under those directories, excluding files whose pre-canonicalization walk-emitted path contains any of the plain substrings '.stories.', '.test.', '.spec.', '__snapshots__', or 'node_modules' (unless a src_dir's configured path string itself contains 'node_modules' as a substring, in which case the 'node_modules' substring exclusion is skipped for that src_dir's walk), excluding any file whose pre-canonicalization walk-emitted path contains a user-supplied entry from options.exclude_patterns as a substring, and, when PipelineOptions.exclude_prefixes is non-empty, excluding any component whose display_name starts with any of its entries (see non_goals for this filter's exact semantics — it is a deliberate, silent, user-opted-in exclusion, not a failure case). Additionally, using only fixture-observable input/output pairs: (1) given a src_dir inside a real git work tree (a `.git` directory present in the src_dir or an ancestor of it) containing a `.gitignore` file (in the src_dir itself or any ancestor directory up to the work tree root) that matches a candidate file, that file is excluded from the output — UNLESS that src_dir's configured path string itself contains 'node_modules' as a substring, in which case NO `.gitignore` file at any level (the src_dir's own, any ancestor's, or any nested directory's within the walk) excludes anything from that src_dir's walk, regardless of whether the src_dir or any directory beneath it has its own `.git` directory: every such file IS included in the output. Separately and independently: when that src_dir's path string contains 'node_modules' AND the src_dir itself has no `.git` directory of its own, `.git/info/exclude` also does not exclude anything for that src_dir's walk — UNLESS some directory nested beneath the src_dir (not the src_dir itself) has its own `.git` directory, in which case that nested subtree's own `.git/info/exclude` file DOES still exclude matching files within that nested subtree specifically. As a negative pair: a src_dir that is physically located inside a node_modules directory on disk, but whose configured path string does NOT contain the substring 'node_modules' (e.g. reached via a relative path or symlink whose literal string doesn't include it), is NOT exempt from any of the above — ordinary `.gitignore`/`.git/info/exclude` behavior (ancestor-.git-gated, as in the non-node_modules case) applies to it. # NAPI binding

**Source:** `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`, `crates/binding/build.rs`

This is the only consumer-facing FFI boundary in the workspace: a thin `cdylib` that Node.js (concretely, a Vite plugin) calls into. It owns no extraction logic — every entry point marshals `JsExtractOptions` into `PipelineOptions` and delegates straight to `oxc_react_docgen_core::pipeline`. Its entire job is getting values across the Rust/JS boundary without ever letting a Rust panic reach the Node process, and without ever handing a caller anything other than a proper JS `Error` on failure.

## The five NAPI entry points

- `extract_all(options) -> String` — cold, one-shot extraction. Runs inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
- `create_session(options) -> u32` — allocates a session ID, builds a `WatchSession`, inserts it into `SESSIONS`. Runs **synchronously on the calling (JS) thread** — no `spawn_blocking`.
- `initialize_session(session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then runs `WatchSession::initialize()` (the first full cold pass). Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `extract_file_incremental(file_path, session_id, options) -> String` — looks up or lazily creates the session, then runs `WatchSession::update_file()`. Runs inside `spawn_blocking`.
- `close_session(session_id) -> ()` — removes the session from `SESSIONS`. Runs synchronously on the calling thread, like `create_session`.

`SESSIONS` is `static SESSIONS: LazyLock<DashMap<u32, Arc<WatchSession>>>` — a single process-wide session table. `initialize_session` and `extract_file_incremental` both tolerate a missing session ID by silently constructing a fresh `WatchSession` from the passed `options` and inserting it (`lib.rs:171-179`, `200-208`) — this is a lazy-recovery path, not an error case, so a caller that races `create_session` against `initialize_session` (or never calls `create_session` at all) still gets a working session rather than an "unknown session ID" error.

## Panic-containment boundary (LOCKED DESIGN DECISION — ADR 0005)

Every one of the five entry points wraps its real body in `oxc_react_docgen_core::panic_guard::contain_panic(label, closure)`. This is not incidental defense — it is a deliberate, documented design decision (`docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md`) with a specific and non-obvious shape:

- **The three `spawn_blocking`-wrapped entry points** (`extract_all`, `initialize_session`, `extract_file_incremental`) put `contain_panic` **inside** the `spawn_blocking` closure, not around it. Before ADR 0005, these three were only accidentally panic-safe: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` happens to catch an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not because anyone decided panic-safety belonged there. Wrapping in `contain_panic` too makes the guarantee a designed one, converts the panic into a `Diagnostic`-derived `napi::Error` message instead of an opaque `JoinError`, and stops being contingent on tokio's internals never changing.
- **`create_session` and `close_session` get `contain_panic` directly**, with no `spawn_blocking` at all, because they run synchronously on the thread the JS call arrived on. Before ADR 0005 these two had **zero** panic protection — not even the accidental kind — documented as an open, unconfirmed risk in `docs/edge-cases.md` P1-9 ("*(Needs verification, not confirmed)*... Whether a panic here crashes the Node process depends on whether napi-rs's codegen auto-wraps in `catch_unwind`"). ADR 0005 closes that gap directly rather than relying on napi-rs's opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute (considered and rejected in the ADR's "Alternatives considered" section, in favor of one mechanism — `contain_panic` — shared across rayon, plugin hooks, and FFI instead of two different ones). **Note for future readers of `docs/edge-cases.md`: P1-9 as currently written is stale** — it describes a state ADR 0005 has since fixed; it should be marked resolved rather than open next time that document is touched.

Do not remove or "simplify away" the `contain_panic` wrapping in `create_session`/`close_session` on the theory that synchronous code "can't really panic" — `next_session_id()`, `WatchSession::new()`, and `PipelineOptions::try_from` all run inside that closure, and `WatchSession::new` is not a leaf function under this crate's own non-negotiables (no `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`, but a *panic* — e.g. an indexing panic or arithmetic overflow in debug builds — is a different failure mode than `unwrap()` and is exactly what `contain_panic` exists to catch regardless of whether the non-negotiables are honored everywhere upstream).

## Why this crate's panic discipline is higher-stakes than `crates/cli`'s

`panic_guard::contain_panic` is shared code — the same function backs rayon `.map()` closures in `pipeline/mod.rs`, `DocgenPlugin` hook calls in `plugin.rs`, and all five entry points here. But the failure mode on the other side of an *uncaught* panic differs by boundary. `crates/cli` is a standalone binary process: an uncaught panic there kills one CLI invocation, and the OS process boundary means nothing else is affected. This crate is a `cdylib` loaded **in-process** into a long-running Node.js server (a Vite dev server, per the doc comments on `create_session`/`initialize_session`/`close_session` referencing `configResolved`/`configureServer`/`buildEnd`). An uncaught Rust panic crossing the FFI boundary here does not fail one call — it is undefined behavior at best and a hard crash of the entire Node process at worst, taking down every other request the dev server was serving. That asymmetry is why `contain_panic` at this boundary is load-bearing in a way it is only "good hygiene" for `crates/cli`: bypass it here and the blast radius is the whole host process, not one invocation.

## Error conversion: everything converges on `napi::Error::from_reason(String)`

Every fallible path in this file — `PipelineOptions::try_from` validation failures, `contain_panic`'s caught-panic `Diagnostic`, `extraction_output_to_json`/`incremental_update_to_json` serialization errors, and `spawn_blocking`'s own `JoinError` — is mapped through `.map_err(|e| napi::Error::from_reason(e.to_string()))` or the equivalent `Err(diag) => Err(napi::Error::from_reason(diag.to_string()))` arm. There is no code path in this file that lets a `Result::Err` propagate to napi-rs's codegen in any form other than `napi::Error`.

**Invariant 1: no Node caller of any of the five entry points can ever receive anything other than a resolved value or a proper JS `Error` — never an opaque crash, never a native panic message, never a bare Rust `Result` leaking through.** This is what makes `extract_all`/`initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s doubled `Result` handling (`spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` outside, `contain_panic`'s `Result<T, Diagnostic>` inside) necessary rather than redundant — two independent failure channels (task-join failure, application-level panic) both have to be funneled into the one JS-visible error type.

**Invariant 2: `reactVersion` never silently defaults.** `TryFrom<JsExtractOptions> for PipelineOptions` (`lib.rs:59-119`) treats every `Option<T>` field as "use `PipelineOptions::default()`" when `None`, *except* `react_version`, which goes through `oxc_react_docgen_core::react_types::parse_react_version(v)` and hard-errors, naming the bad value, if the caller (e.g. via a TypeScript `as any` cast bypassing the `'react18' | 'react19'` `ts_type`) passes something that isn't one of the two accepted strings. This is a deliberate application of CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") at the boundary where TypeScript's type system stops being a real guarantee.

**Invariant 3: `extraPathsJson`/`knownTypeOverridesJson` malformed JSON is a hard `Err`, never a silently-empty map.** Both fields are accepted as raw JSON strings specifically "to avoid napi object complexity" (`lib.rs:50`) — `serde_json::from_str` failure is mapped to an error naming the field (`"extraPaths is not valid JSON: {e}"` / `"knownTypeOverrides is not valid JSON: {e}"`), not swallowed into `Default::default()`. Covered directly by `malformed_extra_paths_json_is_a_hard_error_not_a_silent_empty_map` and its `known_type_overrides` sibling in the test module.

## Session-ID scheme (LOCKED DESIGN DECISION, with an accepted gap)

```rust
fn next_session_id() -> u32 {
    let pid = std::process::id() as u64;
    let counter = NEXT_SESSION_ID.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    // Avoids session-ID collisions across concurrent Vite dev server instances.
    (((pid & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (counter & 0xFFFF)) as u32
}
```

The `u32` session ID is split into two 16-bit halves: the low 16 bits of the OS PID in the high half, a process-local monotonic counter in the low half. This is a deliberate choice, not an arbitrary bit-packing — the comment states its purpose directly: it keeps session IDs from colliding when multiple Vite dev server processes (e.g. two projects being developed in parallel on the same machine) each load this binding and start allocating session IDs from zero independently.

**Invariant 4: within a single process, `next_session_id()` cannot collide until more than 65,536 sessions have been created in that process's lifetime.** The counter half is masked to 16 bits (`& 0xFFFF`), so it wraps after 65,536 allocations and reuses a session ID that may still be live in `SESSIONS`. This is a known, accepted gap, not a live bug: 65,536 `create_session` calls in one long-running dev-server process is far outside realistic usage (one session per Vite dev server run, not per file change — `update_file`/`extract_file_incremental` reuse the existing session ID), so the ADR-0005-era hardening effort scoped this as low-severity and left it as-is rather than widening the ID to `u64` or adding collision detection on insert. Note: this specific collision-probability tradeoff is not separately written up in `docs/edge-cases.md` at the time of writing — the closest existing entries there concern the panic-safety of `create_session`/`close_session` (P1-9, now stale per above), not this counter-wrap scenario; treat this file as the primary citation for it. If this ever needs to be revisited, the fix is a wider ID type or an explicit `SESSIONS.contains_key` retry loop in `next_session_id`, not a redesign of the packing scheme.

## `JsExtractOptions` → `PipelineOptions`: the shape of the boundary

`JsExtractOptions` (`lib.rs:34-55`) is deliberately flat — every field is a primitive, `String`, `Vec<String>`, or `Option` thereof, with two fields (`extra_paths_json`, `known_type_overrides_json`) pushed out to raw JSON strings specifically to dodge napi's object-marshalling complexity for nested maps. `TryFrom<JsExtractOptions> for PipelineOptions` (`Error = String`, not a structured error type) is the single place this flat shape gets reinflated into the richer `PipelineOptions` that `pipeline::extract`/`WatchSession` actually consume. Every one of the five entry points calls this same `TryFrom` before doing anything else — there is no code path that constructs a `PipelineOptions` from `JsExtractOptions` any other way, so a new validation rule (like Invariant 2's `reactVersion` check) added here is guaranteed to apply uniformly across cold extraction, session creation, and session initialization.

Every fallible path in this file — `PipelineOptions::try_from` validation failures, `contain_panic`'s caught-panic `Diagnostic`, `extraction_output_to_json`/`incremental_update_to_json` serialization errors, and `spawn_blocking`'s own `JoinError` — is mapped through `.map_err(|e| napi::Error::from_reason(e.to_string()))` or the equivalent `Err(diag) => Err(napi::Error::from_reason(diag.to_string()))` arm. There is no code path in this file that lets a `Result::Err` propagate to napi-rs's codegen in any form other than `napi::Error`.

**Invariant 1: no Node caller of any of the five entry points can ever receive anything other than a resolved value or a proper JS `Error` — never an opaque crash, never a native panic message, never a bare Rust `Result` leaking through.** This is what makes `extract_all`/`initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s doubled `Result` handling (`spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` outside, `contain_panic`'s `Result<T, Diagnostic>` inside) necessary rather than redundant — two independent failure channels (task-join failure, application-level panic) both have to be funneled into the one JS-visible error type.

**Invariant 2: `reactVersion` never silently defaults.** `TryFrom<JsExtractOptions> for PipelineOptions` (`lib.rs:59-119`) treats every `Option<T>` field as "use `PipelineOptions::default()`" when `None`, *except* `react_version`, which goes through `oxc_react_docgen_core::react_types::parse_react_version(v)` and hard-errors, naming the bad value, if the caller (e.g. via a TypeScript `as any` cast bypassing the `'react18' | 'react19'` `ts_type`) passes something that isn't one of the two accepted strings. This is a deliberate application of CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") at the boundary where TypeScript's type system stops being a real guarantee.

**Invariant 3: `extraPathsJson`/`knownTypeOverridesJson` malformed JSON is a hard `Err`, never a silently-empty map.** Both fields are accepted as raw JSON strings specifically "to avoid napi object complexity" (`lib.rs:50`) — `serde_json::from_str` failure is mapped to an error naming the field (`"extraPaths is not valid JSON: {e}"` / `"knownTypeOverrides is not valid JSON: {e}"`), not swallowed into `Default::default()`. Covered directly by `malformed_extra_paths_json_is_a_hard_error_not_a_silent_empty_map` and its `known_type_overrides` sibling in the test module.

## Session-ID scheme (LOCKED DESIGN DECISION, with an accepted gap)

```rust
fn next_session_id() -> u32 {
    let pid = std::process::id() as u64;
    let counter = NEXT_SESSION_ID.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    // Avoids session-ID collisions across concurrent Vite dev server instances.
    (((pid & 0xFFFF) << 16) | (counter & 0xFFFF)) as u32
}
```

The `u32` session ID is split into two 16-bit halves: the low 16 bits of the OS PID in the high half, a process-local monotonic counter in the low half. This is a deliberate choice, not an arbitrary bit-packing — the comment states its purpose directly: it keeps session IDs from colliding when multiple Vite dev server processes (e.g. two projects being developed in parallel on the same machine) each load this binding and start allocating session IDs from zero independently.

**Invariant 4: within a single process, `next_session_id()` cannot collide until more than 65,536 sessions have been created in that process's lifetime.** The counter half is masked to 16 bits (`& 0xFFFF`), so it wraps after 65,536 allocations and reuses a session ID that may still be live in `SESSIONS`. This is a known, accepted gap, not a live bug: 65,536 `create_session` calls in one long-running dev-server process is far outside realistic usage (one session per Vite dev server run, not per file change — `update_file`/`extract_file_incremental` reuse the existing session ID), so the ADR-0005-era hardening effort scoped this as low-severity and left it as-is rather than widening the ID to `u64` or adding collision detection on insert. Note: this specific collision-probability tradeoff is not separately written up in `docs/edge-cases.md` at the time of writing — the closest existing entries there concern the panic-safety of `create_session`/`close_session` (P1-9, now stale per above), not this counter-wrap scenario; treat this file as the primary citation for it. If this ever needs to be revisited, the fix is a wider ID type or an explicit `SESSIONS.contains_key` retry loop in `next_session_id`, not a redesign of the packing scheme.

## `JsExtractOptions` → `PipelineOptions`: the shape of the boundary

`JsExtractOptions` (`lib.rs:34-55`) is deliberately flat — every field is a primitive, `String`, `Vec<String>`, or `Option` thereof, with two fields (`extra_paths_json`, `known_type_overrides_json`) pushed out to raw JSON strings specifically to dodge napi's object-marshalling complexity for nested maps. `TryFrom<JsExtractOptions> for PipelineOptions` (`Error = String`, not a structured error type) is the single place this flat shape gets reinflated into the richer `PipelineOptions` that `pipeline::extract`/`WatchSession` actually consume. Every one of the five entry points calls this same `TryFrom` before doing anything else — there is no code path that constructs a `PipelineOptions` from `JsExtractOptions` any other way, so a new validation rule (like Invariant 2's `reactVersion` check) added here is guaranteed to apply uniformly across cold extraction, session creation, and session initialization.

Each `PropType` variant the resolver can emit; whether any fixture produces it.

| Kind | Covered by |

| `boolean` | all fixtures |
| `null` | mui, shadcn |
| `unknown` | mui |

| `object` | mantine, **rdt-compat/types** (`raw_string()` renders real fields — `{ key: Type; key2?: Type2 }` — not the literal placeholder `"object"`) |

| `opaque` | **rdt-compat/types** (inline conditional type `T extends A ? B : C`) |

`PipelineOptions.html_attributes` (CLI: `--html-attributes <curated|full|none>`; NAPI: `htmlAttributes: 'curated' | 'full' | 'none'`; config file: `htmlAttributes` in `docgen.config.ts`) controls how much of an inherited HTML element's attribute surface gets exposed:

## HtmlAttributeMode: curated / full / none

`PipelineOptions.html_attributes` (CLI: `--html-attributes <curated|full|none>`; NAPI: `htmlAttributes: 'curated' | 'full' | 'none'`; config file: `htmlAttributes` in `docgen.config.ts`) controls how much of an inherited HTML element's attribute surface gets exposed:

- **Curated (default)** — unchanged original behavior: ~15-20 hand-picked, commonly-documented attributes per element (`onClick`, `disabled`, `aria-*`, etc.) synthesized into `notableInherited`.
- **Full** — actually resolves `@types/react`'s real `HTMLAttributes`/`AriaAttributes`/`DOMAttributes`/`<Element>HTMLAttributes` interface chain (merged into `GlobalSourceData` by the pipeline, looked up by the resolver like any other interface) and merges the real fields directly into `props` — matching how RDT flattens everything into one props map. Verified against a real button: 238 of ~250 real attributes resolve (the remainder is a narrower, separate gap — see below). Costs ~16ms once per 
- **None** — no inherited HTML attributes synthesized at all; own props only.

# Extractor: OXC AST Visiting → SourceData

**Source:** `crates/core/src/extractor/mod.rs`, `component.rs`, `alias.rs`, `interface.rs`, `jsdoc.rs`, `defaults.rs`, `visit.rs`

The extractor is Phase 2a of the pipeline (`OXC parse → SourceData`). It walks one file's AST with OXC's `Visit` trait and produces a `SourceData` — a fully-owned, allocator-free snapshot of everything downstream phases need. It runs per-file, in parallel, with zero cross-file knowledge.

## The output contract: `SourceData`

```rust
pub struct SourceData {
    pub interfaces: FxHashMap<String, CollectedInterface>,      // "path:Name"
    pub type_aliases: FxHashMap<String, CollectedTypeAlias>,    // "path:Name"
    pub type_alias_params: FxHashMap<String, Vec<TypeName>>,    // generic alias type params
    pub interface_type_params: FxHashMap<String, Vec<TypeName>>,// generic interface type params
    pub enums: FxHashMap<String, Vec<EnumEntry>>,
    pub const_arrays: FxHashMap<String, Vec<EnumValue>>,        // resolver-internal only
    pub component_mappings: Vec<ComponentMapping>,              // .tsx only
    pub imports: Vec<ImportBinding>,
    pub exports: Vec<LexedExport>,
    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
}
```

Everything here is `String`/`Vec`/`FxHashMap` of owned data — never a borrowed AST node. This is the whole point of the module (see Invariant 1). The resolver (`resolve_component()`, called in parallel via rayon) consumes `SourceData` merged across files into `GlobalSourceData`; it never touches OXC types.

Two fields are deliberately *not* part of the "real" output surface: `const_arrays` exists only so the resolver can expand `(typeof X)[number]` into a literal union — it's never serialized to `ExtractionOutput`. `type_alias_params`/`interface_type_params` exist purely to let the resolver recognize a bare generic-parameter reference (`TData` inside `interface Foo<TData>`) as "expected, not unresolvable" rather than a genuine miss — see `resolver/chain.rs`.

## Invariants

1. **No AST reference outlives `parse_file()`.** The `Allocator` is created locally in `parse_file` (mod.rs:135) and dropped when it returns (mod.rs:169). `SourceDataCollector` never stores a `&'a TSType` or similar — every AST value it needs is converted to an owned `CollectedType`/`String`/span-derived `String` before being stashed in `self.data`. **This is convention, not compiler-enforced.** `SourceDataCollector<'src>` *does* borrow `source: &'src str` (the raw text, not the AST), which is what makes span-slicing (`self.source[start..end]`) possible without an allocator dependency. Nothing in the type system stops a future contributor from adding a `Vec<&'a TSType>` field to the collector — the rule survives only because every existing extraction path routes through `ts_type_to_collected` (which fully owns its output) before storing anything. A reviewer adding a new extraction path m

2. **Comments are cloned out of the arena immediately.** `ret.program.comments` lives in the arena; `parse_file` converts it to `Vec<OwnedComment>` (span offsets + `is_block`, no borrowed text) *before* `visit_program` runs (mod.rs:160-166). JSDoc lookups then re-slice `self.source` by those saved offsets rather than holding onto the original `Comment` AST nodes.

3. **Component detection follows a fixed do-first-match-wins chain, not a scored/ranked system.** In `visit_variable_declaration` (visit.rs:236-274), for a `.tsx` file with a PascalCase binding: `try_fc_annotation` → `try_forward_ref` → `try_hoc_wrapped` → (if none matched and there's an initializer) `try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component`. First `Some` wins; there is no fallback merge of partial matches from different detectors.

4. **`record_skip` and silence are two deliberately different outcomes, not a spectrum.** `record_skip` (mod.rs:236-247, `DiagnosticCode::SkippedCandidate`, `Info` severity) fires only when a shape is recognizably *close* to a known pattern but missing/malformed a required piece — e.g. a PascalCase `.tsx` binding whose initializer matches none of the four component detectors (visit.rs:254-263), or a PascalCase function declaration with an untyped first param (visit.rs:314-318). A shape that was never a candidate in the first place (a lowercase binding, a zero-param function — visit.rs's own comment on the zero-param case is explicit about this) produces **no diagnostic at all**. Getting this boundary wrong in either direction is a real regression: too eager and `SkippedCandidate` noise drowns real signal in output; too silent and a shape degrades with zero trace, violating non-negotiable

**Status update (2026-08-13):** the 43-task remediation plan derived from this audit (see `root-cause-analysis.md` and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-edge-case-remediation.md`) has landed on `main`. Every P0 and P1 finding below is now fixed, including P0-2 (cache staleness — originally deliberately deferred as an architectural tradeoff, revisited and fixed 2026-08-13, see its entry). The extractor's eight component-shape detection gaps (new component-shape recognition, not diagnostic-discipline fixes) are also now closed — six genuinely new-feature fixes, one narrower in scope than originally proposed (see the `Object.assign` entry), and two that turned out to already be resolved by the later-gated `SPEC-EXTRACTOR-001` before this list was updated. This doc is kept as the historical record of what was found; strikethrough + **FIXED** marks resolved items rather than deleting them, so the audit trail stays intact.

**How to read this doc:** findings are grouped by severity tier first (for prioritization), then by subsystem (for context when doing the actual fix). "Tested?" means an existing test exercises exactly this behavior, not just the surrounding happy path.

---

## Severity tiers


**Pipeline/discovery — all FIXED:**
- ~~`WatchSession::component_cache` is keyed inconsistently between where it's seeded and where it's updated. `initialize()` seeds it from the cold `output.components` map, whose keys already went through Phase 5's same-file duplicate-display-name disambiguation (1st occurrence keys as bare `display_name`; every subsequent occurrence keys as `"<display_name> (<file_path>)"`). `update_file()` inserted re-resolved components keyed by bare `entry.display_name` only, with no disambiguation — two manifestations of the same root cause (`component_cache.insert(entry.display_name.clone(), ...)` was a pure insert, never evicting whatever key(s) that file's components previously occupied): a renamed component left its old-name key behind forever, and — more severely — editing a component that initialize() had disambiguated (because another file already held its bare name) silently overwrote the OTHER file's bare-keyed entry with the edited file's fresh content, while the edited file's own disambiguated key kept its stale pre-edit content.~~ **FIXED** (2026-08-13). `update_file()` now evicts every existing cache entry belonging to the changed file (by whichever key it held) before inserting its freshly-resolved entries, then re-disambiguates against whatever remains — mirroring Phase 5's bare-then-disambiguated rule, checked incrementally instead of via a session-wide counter. Deliberately excludes one case: a failed read (deletion, permission error, non-UTF8 content) does NOT trigger eviction, since AC-019 explicitly specifies a deleted file's stale component should persist in the ca

- ~~Permission-denied files/directories are silently dropped during discovery — `ignore::Walk`'s `Err` results are discarded via `.flatten()`.~~ **FIXED**: walker errors now push a `DiagnosticCode::IoError` diagnostic naming the directory. `discover.rs:17`
- ~~Non-UTF8 filenames are silently dropped during discovery.~~ **FIXED**: a failed `Utf8PathBuf` conversion now pushes a "Skipping non-UTF8 path" diagnostic instead of vanishing. `discover.rs:24,41`
- ~~An explicitly empty `src_dirs` (`[]`...) short-circuits past the "all src dirs missing" diagnostic entirely.~~ **FIXED**: empty `src_dirs` now gets its own explicit "No source directories configured" diagnostic, distinct from the missing-directories case. `pipeline/mod.rs:220,235-238`
## CLI/config — new, previously-untracked bugs (found and fixed 2026-08-12 via Phase 3 spec-drift validation against SPEC-CLI-001b/d)

- **FIXED.** `WatchSession::snapshot()` always returned `stats: ExtractionStats::default()`, so `watch --out`'s written JSON reported `componentsExtracted: 0` (and every other stats field zeroed) regardless of how many components the session actually held — any consumer reading stats from a watch-mode output file was reading zeros. **FIXED**: `components_extracted` is now computed from the real component count; the other stats fields (files_parsed, dts_cache_hits, duration_ms, tier1/tier3/opaque counts) remain a narrower, still-open gap since they describe a single `extract()` run's bookkeeping that this session doesn't accumulate incrementally. Test: `snapshot_stats_components_extracted_reflects_the_real_component_count`. | `pipeline/watch.rs:139` |
- **FIXED.** A relative `--config` path whose parent directory differs from the process's actual cwd failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` even though the file existed (e.g. `--config plain/docgen.config.ts` from the repo root). Root cause: `try_load_config` changes the spawned node subprocess's cwd to the config file's parent (so `tsx`/imports resolve relative to the config, not to wherever the CLI was invoked from), but passed the original *relative* path string through unchanged in `__DOCGEN_CONFIG_PATH` — node then re-resolved that same relative string against the *new* cwd it had just been given. **FIXED**: the path is now canonicalized before being passed to the subprocess, falling back to the original (relative) path if canonicalization fails so a genuine "file not found" error still names what the user typed. Test: `try_load_config_resolves_a_relative_path_whose_parent_is_not_the_cwd`. | `cli/config.rs:112` |

**Watch mode — component_cache staleness, strengthened (2026-08-12):** Phase 3 validation independently reconfirmed the `component_cache` bare-name-vs-disambiguated-key mismatch already tracked above, and found a second manifestation of the same underlying design gap: `update_file` never *evicts* a stale entry when a component is renamed between edits (`Card` renamed to `Panel` leaves both `"Card"` and `"Panel"` present in `component_cache`, since the incremental path only ever inserts under the new key and nothing removes the old one). Both manifestations trace to the same root cause — `component_cache.insert(entry.display_name.clone(), ...)` is a pure insert with no corresponding eviction of whatever key(s) that file's components previously occupied. **Still open** — the fix likely needs `update_file` to track and remove a file's previous component keys before inserting its newly-resolved ones, not just a disambiguation-rule fix.

## LSP — new bug found and fixed 2026-08-12 via Phase 3+ spec-drift validation

Two clusters are genuine new architectural decisions, not enforcement of an existing pattern. Drafted here; write the real `docs/adr/000N-*.md` file as part of implementing that cluster, per the ADR guide's "write it when the decision is made" convention — these are proposals, not yet accepted.

### Proposed: 0005. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary

**Context:** No existing ADR covers panic/unwind policy. Panic safety today is an accident of `tokio::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError`, inconsistent across NAPI entry points, plugin hooks, and rayon batches — `create_session`/`close_session` don't even get that accidental protection, and `watch.rs`'s `std::sync::Mutex` can poison permanently as a direct consequence. Picking the wrong granularity now (per-batch vs. per-file vs. per-plugin) is expensive to fix retroactively once call sites depend on 

**Decision:** Panics reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook, or a NAPI entry point are contained at per-file/per-plugin/per-call granularity through one sanctioned helper, `panic_guard::contain_panic`, converting the payload into a `Diagnostic` (or `napi::Error`) instead of aborting a batch, killing the whole pipeline, or poisoning a session lock. `contain_panic` wraps its closure in `AssertUnwindSafe` internally (documented rationale: this codebase's data has no interior mutabil

**Consequences:**
- One bad file, plugin, or session call degrades to a diagnostic instead of taking down everything sharing its batch/pipeline/session.
- Every future concurrent, plugin, or FFI entry point has one obvious place to route through, instead of re-deriving the answer.
- `watch.rs`'s poisoned-mutex trap becomes structurally much less likely, since nothing panics while the lock is held anymore.

### Proposed: 0006. Derive JSON Schema instead of hand-writing it

**Context:** `schema.rs`'s hand-written schema has already drifted from `ComponentEntry`/`ExtractionStats`/`Diagnostic`'s real fields, undetected because the only test checks JSON syntax validity, not field-set parity. ADR-0002 already established the precedent of hand-writing `Serialize` for the three recursive enums (`PropType`, `CollectedType`, `OpaqueReason`) to avoid a recursion-limit blowup.

**Decision:** Derive `schemars::JsonSchema` on the plain output structs, including `OpaqueReason` (verified non-recursive, already using an ordinary `derive` for `Serialize` — not one of the hand-written cases despite ADR-0002's text suggesting otherwise); hand-write matching `JsonSchema` impls only for `PropType` and `CollectedType`, the two enums that are actually recursive and actually hand-write `Serialize` today. `cmd_schema()` calls `schemars::schema_for!(ExtractionOutput)` instead of buil

**Consequences:**
- A second hand-maintained trait impl per recursive enum whenever a variant is added — the same "compiler won't remind you" tradeoff ADR-0002 already accepted for `Serialize`, now doubled. Scoped to 2 enums (`PropType`, `CollectedType`), not 3.
- Every plain-struct field addition is schema-correct automatically; only the two recursive enums need manual attention going forward.
- New dependency (`schemars`) — if that's undesirable, the floor-level alternative is a CI test that serializes a real fixture and validates it against the hand-written schema, catching drift without adding a dependency.

AST visiting and component-shape detection (extractor crate) — not specified here.
Type resolution semantics, e.g. how a prop type is resolved from a TS type node (resolver crate) — not specified here.
CLI argument parsing, terminal/progress output formatting, or config-file loading (crates/cli) — not specified here.
NAPI/Node session lifecycle and binding-layer error translation (crates/binding) — not specified here.
Closing the DTS cache's known mtime+size same-tick staleness gap. This spec requires that the gap be documented and bounded (scoped to .d.ts files only, cache.rs), not that it be fixed — a content-hash or fast-hash based fix is an explicit non-goal of this spec per the locked design decision in the pipeline-orchestration reference.
Making ReverseDeps incrementally update within a live watch session as imports change, or pruning WatchSession::component_cache when a file is deleted mid-session. Both are the same class of documented, deliberately deferred staleness: this spec requires the session's currently-observed behavior be specified accurately (see AC-019), not that either gap be closed within a session's lifetime short of restart.
Extending plugin hooks (on_file_extracted/on_component_resolved) to run during WatchSession::update_file(). Today they run only in the cold extract()/initialize() path — this spec does not require update_file() to invoke plugins.
watch --out file-write atomicity and error surfacing — that is CLI-layer behavior (crates/cli/src/commands/watch.rs), not part of this pipeline contract.
Explaining or naming the `ignore` crate's internal gating mechanism (flags, precedence rules between VCS-ignore sources, or whether a directory 'has_git'/'is inside a git work tree' by internal detection) beyond what AC-001 itself asserts as fixture-observable input/output pairs. AC-001 is written entirely in terms of real .gitignore/.ignore/.git/info/exclude fixture layouts and extract()'s output — a tester needs no knowledge of the `ignore` crate's internals to check it.
Testing the machine-global gitignore (core.excludesFile) sub-case specifically — no test fixture can construct a machine-global gitignore in isolation, so this spec does not require a fixture-level pair for it; the concept is referenced only in describing what is disabled by the node_modules exception, not as an independently fixture-tested clause.
Documenting exclude_prefixes' full matching semantics (start-of-string vs. substring) or its lack of a per-skip diagnostic as a gap. Like exclude_patterns, this is a deliberate, silent, user-opted-in filter (see PipelineOptions.exclude_prefixes doc comment: 'Component name prefixes to skip') — a user who configures it is intentionally removing components from output, which is not the kind of undetectable failure CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #6 is about.
pipeline::extract(), pipeline::PipelineOptions, pipeline::WatchSession (new/initialize/update_file/snapshot), pipeline::discover_files, the DTS parse cache's staleness contract as observed through extraction output, and panic containment as observed at the file/component/plugin granularity. Covers only externally observable behavior of these entry points — not internal phase implementation. This document's own phase numbering, used by several criteria below, is: Discover(1) -> Parse(2) -> Merge(3, with an optional 3.5 sub-step that merges @types/react when html_attributes == HtmlAttributeMode::Full, and a 3.6 sub-step that merges ambient TS lib files unconditionally) -> Resolve(4) -> Collect/dedup(5). Component output key disambiguation rule, also referenced by multiple criteria below: within a single extraction run, the first resolved occurrence of a given display_name keys as the bare display_name; every subsequent occurrence of that same display_name keys as "<display_name> (<file_path>)".

## 2. How ParsedProp fields are populated; PropType variants

### ParsedProp.parent and .declarations
- Interface and alias-chain props (chain.rs:245, 278-287):
  - `parent = PropParent{ name: iface.name, file_name: iface.file_path }`.
  - Passed as `Some(parent.clone())` and `vec![parent.clone()]`.
  - `declarations` is always a single element equal to `parent`. It is never merged.
  - The doc comment at output.rs:137 ("for overloads/merging") is not backed by any merging code I found.
  - `record_variant_props` (alias.rs:409-429) keeps only the first-seen prop clone.
- Inline object literal in an intersection or an `__anon_N` alias (alias.rs:198-207): `default=None`, `tags=empty`, `parent=None`, `declarations=[]`.
- Known-pattern props (known.rs:292-302 `simple_prop`; CVA/VariantProps, RenderProps, SlotProps): `parent=None`, `declarations=[]`.
- `notable_inherited` synthesized props (resolver/mod.rs:317-329):
  - `parent = {"<Cap>HTMLAttributes", "node_modules/@types/react/index.d.ts"}`, `declarations=[]`.
  - Types are name-guessed by `infer_html_attr_prop_type` (html.rs:5-21). Handlers become `EventHandler{event_type:"Event"}`.
  - For any element other than a few, `<Cap>` is `"HTML"`, so `parent.name` is `HTMLHTMLAttributes`. This is in committed snapshot chakra.snap:855.

### .description and .tags
- Extractor JSDoc from the property signature (extractor/mod.rs:736, 750), via jsdoc.rs `find_jsdoc_with_tags`, copied verbatim.

### .default_value
- Sources:
  - Destructured params: defaults.rs:13-45, `eval_expr_as_default`.
    - Literals give `computed:false`.
    - Array and object literals keep their source text.
    - Everything else has `computed:true`.
  - Static `X.defaultProps = {..}` (interface.rs:221-243), merged into `mapping.param_defaults`.
  - JSDoc `@default` or `@defaultValue` from `RawProp.tags`.
- Precedence at chain.rs:251-276: code wins over JSDoc. A mismatch pushes an Info `JsDocDefaultMismatch`.
- `param_defaults` is per component, keyed by prop name.
  - It is applied to every interface prop of that name, including inherited ones (chain.rs:251).
  - It is never applied to inline-object props (alias.rs:200).
- `memo(forwardRef<..>(..))` sets `param_defaults: Default::default()` (component.rs ~205-220).

### Prop merge order [CR]
- resolver/mod.rs:288-292 says "own props win over inherited props with same name" but uses `props.entry(name).or_insert(prop)` over `chain.props`.
- In `resolve_interface_chain`, `merge_parent` for extends runs before own props are pushed (chain.rs ~222-290).
- So for `interface B extends A { x: ... }` the parent's `x` appears first and wins.
- I found no test for a child re-declaring a parent's prop. Not executed.

### PropType (output.rs:238-314, 27 variants; wire `kind` in parentheses)
- Primitives:
  - `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Null`, `Undefined`, `Any`, `Never`, `Unknown`, `Void`. Direct TS primitive keywords.
- Literals:
  - `StringLiteral(String)`, `NumberLiteral(f64)`, `BoolLiteral(bool)`.
  - Non-finite numbers are encoded as the strings "NaN", "Infinity" and "-Infinity" (output.rs:470-486).
- Composites:
  - `Union(Vec)`, `Intersection(Vec)`, `Array(Box)`, `Tuple(Vec)`.
  - `Object(Vec<ObjectField>)` is an inline object type with `{name, prop_type, required, description}` only.
- `Named{name: CompactString, args}` is a name-only reference to an unexpanded type. It carries no file or symbol identity.
- `ReactNode` is ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, ReactPortal, ReactFragment and ReactChild collapsed together (react.rs:19-23).
- `CssProperties` covers CSSProperties and CSSObject.
- `EventHandler{event_type: String, param_name}`:
  - Any single-parameter function type or `*Handler` name.
  - A zero-argument function has `event_type:"void"`.
  - It has no return-type field (func.rs:31-52).
- `Ref{element: Option<String>}`.
- `ElementType` is `React.ElementType`, used for polymorphic `as` and `component` props.
- `HtmlAttributes{element, omitted}` is a marker for `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'x'>`-style attribute inheritance.
- `LiteralUnion{members: Vec<String>, has_default}` is a union of string literals from an alias, enum, const array, cva, or expanded template literal.
  - The same TS type inline is `Union[StringLiteral..]`.
- `SxProps` is a name-based shortcut for MUI `SxProps`, `SystemStyleObject` and `SystemCssProperties` (known.rs:97).
- `Opaque(OpaqueDetail{raw: String, reason})` is the give-up result.

### Variants with no natural checker-Type counterpart
- **Opaque**: it carries only a raw string plus a reason, no structure. It is exactly where enrichment would replace a value.
- **SxProps**: a name-matched marker, not a structural type. It also matches by name only.
- **HtmlAttributes**: element metadata, not a type. The real expansion depends on `HtmlAttributeMode` (Curated, Full or None; pipeline/mod.rs:52-66).
- **Named**: it has no symbol, declaration or file identity. Generic args are `PropType`.
- **ReactNode, CssProperties, ElementType, Ref, EventHandler**: name-based collapses of declared React types.
  - `Ref` keeps only a string element.
  - `EventHandler` drops return type and any second parameter.
- **LiteralUnion**: `members` are display strings. Numbers and booleans from enums are stringified via `to_display_string`, so type information is lost.
- **Object**: no optional or readonly distinction beyond `required`, and no index signatures, call signatures, or method-versus-property distinction.
- **Tuple**: elements only. There is no optional, rest or named-element info.
- TS shapes with no variant:
  - bigint and symbol become `Named`.
  - Enum types: no variant.
  - Multi-parameter functions become Opaque(MultiParamFunction) (func.rs:55-80).
  - Readonly and unique operators are peeled by the extractor.
  - `undefined` inside a union is dropped by `resolve_union` (primitives.rs:19-21).
  - `typeof X` becomes `Named`.

## 3. RDT projection

Code: `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:94-125` (`serialize_rdt`) and `76-90` (`rdt_type_json`). Grep found no other producer.

Emitted per component (top-level is a JSON object keyed by the `output.components` key):
| RDT field | Derived from | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| top-level key | `components` key | Bare display name, or `"Name (path)"` for 2nd+ same-named. |
| `displayName` | `entry.display_name` | 1:1 |
| `description` | `entry.description` | 1:1 |
| `methods` | hardcoded `[]` | Locked decision. |
| `tags` | `entry.tags` | Component-level tags. |
| `composes` | `entry.composes` | Conflates RDT-native composition with resolver give-ups. |
| `props` | `entry.props` map | `notable_inherited` is not included. |

Emitted per prop:
| RDT field | Derived from |
|---|---|
| `name` | `prop.name` |
| `type` | `rdt_type_json(prop.prop_type)` |
| `required` | `prop.required` |
| `defaultValue` | `{value, computed}` or null |
| `description` | `prop.description` |
| `parent` | `{name, fileName}` or null |

- `rdt_type_json` output, for a `type` object:
  - `{name:"enum", value:[{value:..}]}` iff `is_literal_union()` (2+ literal members).
  - Otherwise `{name: raw_string()}`.
  - **No `type.raw` is emitted.**

Not emitted in RDT:
- prop `tags` (every `@deprecated` and `@since` on props is lost) and prop `declarations`
- `filePath`, `inheritance`, `notableInherited`, `discriminantProp`
- top-level `enums`, `diagnostics` and `stats`
- `OpaqueReason`

Storybook (extract.rs:127-155): `type` is always `{name: raw_string()}`. `defaultValue` is `{value}` only. There is no `parent` and no `composes`.

Lossy or not derivable from canonical:
- `type.name` flattens all structure to a string via `raw_string()` (output.rs:379-433).
  - It cannot distinguish `PropType::SxProps` from `Named{SxProps}`.
  - It loses `OpaqueReason`.
  - It loses `LiteralUnion.has_default`.
  - It drops `Object` field descriptions.
  - Unions are joined with " | " with no parentheses.
- `EventHandler` with `param_name: None` prints `(e: X) => void`. The `e` is synthesized (output.rs:421-423).
- `HtmlAttributes` prints `format!("{}HTMLAttributes", element_to_type_name(element))` (output.rs:427-429, 717-730).
  - Only button, input, textarea, select, a, form, label and img have their own names.
  - Everything else, including div, gives "HTML", so div becomes `HTMLHTMLAttributes`.
- 0- or 1-member literal unions never get the enum shape. This is intentional.
- Curated HTML attributes live in `notable_inherited`, so they are invisible in RDT and Storybook unless Full mode merged them into `props`.
- `parent` reduces to `{name, fileName}`.

## 4. Watch and incremental model

Files: `crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs`, and `ReverseDeps` at `pipeline/mod.rs:143-187`.

### `update_file` flow (watch.rs:165-345)
1. Canonicalize the path (`canonicalize_best_effort`, line 175).
2. Read and re-parse only the changed file and cache it in `source_cache` (179-188). There is no DTS cache use here.
3. `global.rcu`: deep-clone the entire `GlobalSourceData`, then `remove_file` and `merge` the new data (196-201).
4. Patch `NamedTypeIndex` in place under a Mutex via `Arc::make_mut` (211-217).
5. `affected = reverse_deps.load().affected(changed)` (220). This is a BFS over file-level reverse imports.
6. `affected_mappings` = every `ComponentMapping` whose `m.file_path` is in `affected` (227-228).
7. Build a fresh `ResolutionContext`, then `par_iter` with `contain_panic` per component (231-270).
8. Evict `component_cache` entries with `file_path == changed`, unless the read failed (295-305).
9. Insert results with a disambiguation check (307-329).
10. Replace the per-file diagnostics entry (333-337).

### Dependency granularity
- **There is no per-component input-file or dependency set.**
  - Selection is file-level.
  - `ResolveState.visited` and `named_in_progress` are discarded after `resolve_component`.
  - `PropParent.file_name` and `InheritedLayer.file_name` are output provenance, not used for invalidation.
- `ReverseDeps::build` (pipeline/mod.rs:149-169):
  - It reads only `global.import_map` (line 152).
  - Only relative specifiers count (155).
  - It probes `.ts`, `.tsx`, `/index.ts` and `/index.tsx` by lexical `join`, with no I/O (159).
  - `re_export_map` is not consulted, so `export * from` barrels create no edges. `..` segments are not normalized. [CR]
- `reverse_deps` is stored once at `initialize()` (watch.rs:123) and never rebuilt.
  - The struct doc (watch.rs:41-46) states it "does not track incremental import-graph edits within a session".
  - Add or remove imports and the graph stays stale until a new session.
- `IncrementalUpdate.affected_files` returns the affected file set.

### Caches and invalidation
| Cache | Key | Invalidated by |
|---|---|---|
| `DtsCache` (cache.rs:92-96, `DashMap<CacheKey,SourceData>`) | `(path, FxHasher content hash)` (51-61) | A different content hash creates a new key. |
| `source_cache` | file path | Overwritten each update. Never read anywhere else (grep shows only inserts). |
| `component_cache` | display name, or `"Name (path)"` | Only the changed file's own entries are evicted. |
| `diagnostics` | changed file path | Replaced (not appended) on each `update_file`. |
| `named_types` `Mutex<Arc<NamedTypeIndex>>` | `(file, name)` | Patched per file. |

DTS cache details:
- It is used only for `.d.ts` files, in `extract_with_global` (pipeline/mod.rs:273, 299-320) and `merge_cached_dts_file` (531-548).
- It has the same key and the same cache handle in the cold path only. `update_file` bypasses it entirely.
- The manifest has only `schema` and `entry_count` (cache.rs:206-210). There is no extractor or crate version, so extractor logic changes without a `SourceData` shape change do not invalidate.
- `insert` (151-162) never removes older-hash entries for the same path.
- When 5000 entries are reached, it evicts the first 100 by map iteration order.
- Save is atomic for the data file (temp + rename). The manifest is written non-atomically afterwards.

Per-call rebuild costs in `update_file`:
- `ResolutionContext::build` (resolver/mod.rs:178-219) rebuilds the following on every call:
  - `ImportResolutionMap`
  - enum and const-array indexes
  - a new `oxc_resolver::Resolver` (so its filesystem cache is discarded)
  - a tsconfig-paths read (line 184)
- Only `ambient_global_files` (a OnceLock) and `named_types` are kept incrementally.

- `param_defaults` is per component, keyed by prop name.
  - It is applied to every interface prop of that name, including inherited ones (chain.rs:251).
  - It is never applied to inline-object props (alias.rs:200).
- `memo(forwardRef<..>(..))` sets `param_defaults: Default::default()` (component.rs ~205-220).

### Prop merge order [CR]
- resolver/mod.rs:288-292 says "own props win over inherited props with same name" but uses `props.entry(name).or_insert(prop)` over `chain.props`.
- In `resolve_interface_chain`, `merge_parent` for extends runs before own props are pushed (chain.rs ~222-290).
- So for `interface B extends A { x: ... }` the parent's `x` appears first and wins.

### PropType (output.rs:238-314, 27 variants; wire `kind` in parentheses)
- Primitives:
  - `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Null`, `Undefined`, `Any`, `Never`, `Unknown`, `Void`. Direct TS primitive keywords.
- Literals:
  - `StringLiteral(String)`, `NumberLiteral(f64)`, `BoolLiteral(bool)`.
  - Non-finite numbers are encoded as the strings "NaN", "Infinity" and "-Infinity" (output.rs:470-486).
- Composites:
  - `Union(Vec)`, `Intersection(Vec)`, `Array(Box)`, `Tuple(Vec)`.
  - `Object(Vec<ObjectField>)` is an inline object type with `{name, prop_type, required, description}` only.
- `Named{name: CompactString, args}` is a name-only reference to an unexpanded type. It carries no file or symbol identity.
- `ReactNode` is ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, ReactPortal, ReactFragment and ReactChild collapsed together (react.rs:19-23).
- `CssProperties` covers CSSProperties and CSSObject.
- `EventHandler{event_type: String, param_name}`:
  - Any single-parameter function type or `*Handler` name.
  - A zero-argument function has `event_type:"void"`.
  - It has no return-type field (func.rs:31-52).
- `Ref{element: Option<String>}`.
- `ElementType` is `React.ElementType`, used for polymorphic `as` and `component` props.
- `HtmlAttributes{element, omitted}` is a marker for `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'x'>`-style attribute inheritance.
- `LiteralUnion{members: Vec<String>, has_default}` is a union of string literals from an alias, enum, const array, cva, or expanded template literal.
  - The same TS type inline is `Union[StringLiteral..]`.
- `SxProps` is a name-based shortcut for MUI `SxProps`, `SystemStyleObject` and `SystemCssProperties` (known.rs:97).
- `Opaque(OpaqueDetail{raw: String, reason})` is the give-up result.

### Variants with no natural checker-Type counterpart
- **Opaque**: it carries only a raw string plus a reason, no structure. It is exactly where enrichment would replace a value.
- **SxProps**: a name-matched marker, not a structural type. It also matches by name only.
- **HtmlAttributes**: element metadata, not a type. The real expansion depends on `HtmlAttributeMode` (Curated, Full or None; pipeline/mod.rs:52-66).
- **Named**: it has no symbol, declaration or file identity. Generic args are `PropType`.
- **ReactNode, CssProperties, ElementType, Ref, EventHandler**: name-based collapses of declared React types.
  - `Ref` keeps only a string element.
  - `EventHandler` drops return type and any second parameter.
- **LiteralUnion**: `members` are display strings. Numbers and booleans from enums are stringified via `to_display_string`, so type information is lost.
- **Object**: no optional or readonly distinction beyond `required`, and no index signatures, call signatures, or method-versus-property distinction.
- **Tuple**: elements only. There is no optional, rest or named-element info.
- TS shapes with no variant:
  - bigint and symbol become `Named`.
  - Enum types: no variant.
  - Multi-parameter functions become Opaque(MultiParamFunction) (func.rs:55-80).
  - Readonly and unique operators are peeled by the extractor.
  - `undefined` inside a union is dropped by `resolve_union` (primitives.rs:19-21).
  - `typeof X` becomes `Named`.

## 3. RDT projection

Code: `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:94-125` (`serialize_rdt`) and `76-90` (`rdt_type_json`). Grep found no other producer.

Emitted per component (top-level is a JSON object keyed by the `output.components` key):
| RDT field | Derived from | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| top-level key | `components` key | Bare display name, or `"Name (path)"` for 2nd+ same-named. |
| `displayName` | `entry.display_name` | 1:1 |
| `description` | `entry.description` | 1:1 |
| `methods` | hardcoded `[]` | Locked decision. |
| `tags` | `entry.tags` | Component-level tags. |
| `composes` | `entry.composes` | Conflates RDT-native composition with resolver give-ups. |
| `props` | `entry.props` map | `notable_inherited` is not included. |

Emitted per prop:
| RDT field | Derived from |
|---|---|
| `name` | `prop.name` |
| `type` | `rdt_type_json(prop.prop_type)` |
| `required` | `prop.required` |
| `defaultValue` | `{value, computed}` or null |
| `description` | `prop.description` |
| `parent` | `{name, fileName}` or null |

- `rdt_type_json` output, for a `type` object:
  - `{name:"enum", value:[{value:..}]}` iff `is_literal_union()` (2+ literal members).
  - Otherwise `{name: raw_string()}`.
  - **No `type.raw` is emitted.**

Not emitted in RDT:
- prop `tags` (every `@deprecated` and `@since` on props is lost) and prop `declarations`
- `filePath`, `inheritance`, `notableInherited`, `discriminantProp`
- top-level `enums`, `diagnostics` and `stats`
- `OpaqueReason`

Storybook (extract.rs:127-155): `type` is always `{name: raw_string()}`. `defaultValue` is `{value}` only. There is no `parent` and no `composes`.

Lossy or not derivable from canonical:
- `type.name` flattens all structure to a string via `raw_string()` (output.rs:379-433).
  - It cannot distinguish `PropType::SxProps` from `Named{SxProps}`.
  - It loses `OpaqueReason`.
  - It loses `LiteralUnion.has_default`.
  - It drops `Object` field descriptions.
  - Unions are joined with " | " with no parentheses.
- `EventHandler` with `param_name: None` prints `(e: X) => void`. The `e` is synthesized (output.rs:421-423).
- `HtmlAttributes` prints `format!("{}HTMLAttributes", element_to_type_name(element))` (output.rs:427-429, 717-730).
  - Only button, input, textarea, select, a, form, label and img have their own names.
  - Everything else, including div, gives "HTML", so div becomes `HTMLHTMLAttributes`.
- 0- or 1-member literal unions never get the enum shape. This is intentional.
- Curated HTML attributes live in `notable_inherited`, so they are invisible in RDT and Storybook unless Full mode merged them into `props`.
- `parent` reduces to `{name, fileName}`.
